clue.text: Skull, perhaps — or nut?

definitions.meaning: the skull is the bony container that encloses the brain, a box for what sits on your neck
slang for a crazy or eccentric person

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description of the bony box round the brain, and a slang synonym for an eccentric or mad person.

clue.text: Establishment for the young flying fish?

parts.note: something flying is up in the air, so high
a school is a large group of fish swimming together

explanation.surface: Somewhere that rears young flying fish, like a hatchery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a school is a group of fish rather than a single fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a place where teenagers are educated.

clue.text: Rule left to the last — it's boring

indicators.note: says the letter for left is shifted along to the final position of the word

parts.note: a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A tedious regulation that everyone puts off dealing with until the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the last' sends the L of LAW to the end. 'Boring' is literal: the tool makes holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed tool that pierces holes in leather or wood, so it literally bores.

clue.text: Lament welcoming possible scum to Canadian city

indicators.note: the word for lament welcomes the other in, taking it inside itself

parts.note: to cry is to lament
an alga can form the green scum on a pond, hence 'possible'

explanation.surface: Someone bemoans a Canadian city letting in undesirable people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scum' reads as low-life people being let into the country, but it is the green film on a pond; 'welcoming' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is the largest city in the province of Alberta.

clue.text: Old, extraordinarily loud dresses, raciest sort of clothes for one in the military

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap round it, so the rearranged letters go outside
to sort letters is to put them in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the loud marking dresses the letter for old, covering it on both sides

parts.note: ff is the musical marking for very loud, so ffff is extraordinarily loud

explanation.surface: Garish old frocks are the most daring outfits a serviceman could wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dresses' makes FFOFF and 'sort of' makes STAICER, which 'clothes' wraps round it. The surface is all frocks, yet 'dresses' and 'clothes' are both verbs of covering.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a commissioned soldier who assists a commander with administration and planning.

clue.text: In order, articles passed round

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the two articles are passed round the honour, enclosing it

parts.note: THE is the definite article
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Items are handed about a group in the proper sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The tiny first word is the whole definition. 'In order' looks like one phrase but splits, and 'passed round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: if you are in, you have not gone out of your house.

clue.text: Popular protector of part of the chest that's taken in air

indicators.note: the chest bone is taken inside the word for a melody

parts.note: an air is a melody, a tune
a rib is one of the bones of the chest

explanation.surface: A well-liked chest guard that has somehow absorbed air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular' means 'of the people', not well-liked, and 'air' is a melody rather than breath; 'that's taken in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome this official was elected to defend the rights of the common people.

clue.text: Passing comments round was effective — a direct hit

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape
something that bit took effect, as sanctions or cuts do

indicators.note: striking the letters knocks them into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A round of casual remarks landed squarely on its target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' rearranges A DIRECT into ERDICTA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal term for remarks a judge makes in passing, not essential to the ruling.

clue.text: Before blowing up, it may produce steam and ash

definitions.text: it may produce steam and ash

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: ante is the Latin prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: A volcano gives off steam and ash ahead of an eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing up' turns ANTE upwards in this down entry; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the active Sicilian volcano emits vapour and cinders.

clue.text: Girl, single, poor Christian

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
I looks like the numeral one, a single
lean means meagre or poor, as in lean years

explanation.surface: An unmarried, penniless young woman of the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a follower of Jesus, who came from that region of Palestine.

clue.text: Subordinate attired 60s style?

parts.note: the mini skirt was the fashion of the 1960s
if you are attired in a garment you have it on

explanation.surface: A junior employee dressed in the fashion of the 1960s.
explanation.walkthrough: Having a mini on is being dressed 60s style; the question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an underling who serves someone more powerful.

clue.text: Infant prodigy? That's no surprise!

definitions.meaning: a small marvel, read whimsically as a gifted child
the exclamation meaning it is hardly astonishing

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description of a tiny marvel, and an idiom meaning something is hardly astonishing.

clue.text: Remarkable loss that stops one in one's tracks?

definitions.text: that stops one in one's tracks?

parts.note: signal as an adjective means notable, as in a signal achievement
a loss is a defeat, a failure

explanation.surface: A defeat so striking that it brings you to a dead halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The tracks are railway lines: this fault is a notorious cause of British train delays.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway fault that halts trains on the line, which is the literal sense of the idiom.

clue.text: Early bonus, then work to maintain the misery of days gone by?

indicators.note: to maintain is to keep or hold, so the short word holds the rest inside

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does
olden means of former times
hell is a state of misery

explanation.surface: A new hire gets a payment up front, then must toil on as wretchedly as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to maintain' has GO holding OLDEN HELL, the misery of days gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment made to a new employee on joining a firm, so a reward paid at the start.

clue.text: Unfaithful type violently slated? Sure

indicators.note: violence throws the letters about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Was the cheating partner fiercely criticised? Certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' rearranges SLATED and SURE together.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a married woman who has an affair.

clue.text: Plant entirely lacking in leadership

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so that letter is missing

parts.note: wholly means entirely

explanation.surface: A factory completely without anyone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in leadership' takes the W off WHOLLY. The plant looks like a factory but is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an evergreen shrub with prickly leaves and red berries.

clue.text: Stupid craze hooking the assistant, I disregarded

indicators.note: to hook is to catch, so the craze catches the rest inside it

parts.note: a fad is a passing craze
taken as written

indicators.note: the letter I is ignored, so left out of the word for assistant

parts.note: an aide is an assistant
taken as written

explanation.surface: I ignored a silly fashion that had ensnared my helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarded' leaves ADE, which with the article before it sits inside the craze, as 'hooking' says. 'I' is the letter, not the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an informal adjective for dim-witted.

clue.text: Cricketing terms for a state of intense activity

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end
in cricket a drive is a firm straight-batted attacking stroke

explanation.surface: The jargon cricketers use for a frantic spell of play.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to go into this is to work at a furious pace, like a car's extra gear.

clue.text: Pot required to feed face daily

indicators.note: to feed something is to go into it, so the pot goes inside the other word

parts.note: the dial is the face of a clock or watch
an urn is a kind of pot or vase

explanation.surface: A cooking pot is needed to keep someone fed every day.
explanation.walkthrough: The face is a clock's, not a person's, so 'feed face' is not about eating; 'required to feed' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: happening every day, or active in the daytime.

clue.text: Noble double century secured

indicators.note: the word for double has secured, that is taken hold of, the letter for century

parts.note: dual means double or twofold
C is the abbreviation for century, as in a cricket score of a hundred

explanation.surface: A batsman reaches a splendid two hundred runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured' puts C inside DUAL. A double century is 200 runs in cricket, but here the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a duke, a high rank of the aristocracy.

clue.text: Useless thing having no say about feeling of resentment

parts.note: a dud is something that does not work

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the two short pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
eg means for example, as does 'say'

explanation.surface: A worthless object with no voice broods on its grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no say' reads as one phrase meaning voiceless, but it splits into two pieces that 'about' turns into GEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym for indignation, as in the phrase 'in high' this.

clue.text: Within one's dwelling, handle so unfamiliar at first? That's unlikely!

definitions.text: Within one's dwelling, handle so unfamiliar at first? That's unlikely!

indicators.note: the rest of the letters go inside the word for one's dwelling

parts.note: your home is where you dwell

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used
something unlikely is odd or improbable, so the letters are in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Under your own roof, would such a moniker really be unknown to begin with? Hardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives U, 'That's unlikely' makes SEHOLDNA and 'Within' places both. Handle is slang for a moniker, so the whole clue also defines: a famous one is never strange indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A person so famous that everybody knows them, so their moniker would hardly be strange indoors.

clue.text: Female under small boat

indicators.note: in a down clue, the female goes below the letter for small

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cow is the female of cattle, elephants and whales

explanation.surface: A woman is trapped beneath a little dinghy.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a flat-bottomed vessel used for carrying cargo.

clue.text: Community: unknown

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed in the clue is a colon, and its name is spelt out
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A label reading 'community', with its details not known.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation mark is not decoration: it is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a settlement or group of people living together.

clue.text: Man's in a bad place — that's binding

indicators.note: the letters for 'man is' go inside the other two pieces

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club
'man is' can be said as 'he's', written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A fellow is stuck somewhere awful, tied by an obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Binding' looks like a contract term but means sticky. The apostrophe in 'Man's' hides 'man is', and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as an adjective: sticky, holding things together.

clue.text: Nazi regalia, not all the rage

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the two words before it are used, a run in the middle

explanation.surface: Fascist insignia are not at all fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' takes a run of letters across the two words before it. 'All the rage' means fashionable, but the phrase splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a more literary word for anger.

clue.text: Unclear this is perfect for the winter?

definitions.meaning: vague or fuzzy, as of thinking

definitions.text: this is perfect for the winter?
definitions.meaning: a British informal word for a knitted jumper (a sweater), ideal in cold weather

explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for vague or fuzzy thinking, and a British informal noun for a knitted sweater worn when it is cold.

clue.text: Worth admitting name at front of ship is royal

indicators.note: the first part is placed before the letters for ship
the word for worth admits, that is lets in, the letter for name

parts.note: the price of something is what it is worth
SS stands for steamship, the prefix on ship names

explanation.surface: It is fitting to concede that the title painted on the bow belongs to the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at front of ship' seems to locate a painted title on the bow, but 'admitting' and 'at front of' are both positional signals and 'royal' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a king's daughter is a member of the royal family, a royal as a noun.
